issues.title: Coroutine state transform `check_must_not_suspend_ty` ignores allocator field of `Box`
issues.body:
This code here has a potential issue:

https://github.com/rust-lang/rust/blob/010f3944e0f0baac8d738da49772fd06acd3701b/compiler/rustc_mir_transform/src/coroutine.rs#L1967-L1977

If the Box has a custom allocator, then that will not be checked at all. So whatever `check_must_not_suspend_ty` is used for, it ignores anything stored in custom allocators.

It seems like this is just for a lint, so this is probably not critical, but I guess should still be fixed.

Cc @cjgillot -- not sure whom else to ping for coroutine state machine transform things?

analysis.originalLogic: In `check_must_not_suspend_ty`, the box arm matched `ty::Adt(..) if ty.is_box()` and then inspected only the boxed element via `let boxed_ty = ty.boxed_ty();`, recursing with `SuspendCheckData { descr_pre, ..data }` where `descr_pre` was built with the `"{}boxed "` prefix.
analysis.incorrectTransformation: The historical transformation treated a `Box<T, A>` as needing a must-not-suspend check only for `T` and never visited the allocator type parameter `A`. It discarded the `GenericArgs` in `ty::Adt(..)` and used `ty.boxed_ty()`, so an `A` annotated `#[must_not_suspend]` was invisible to the lint. The fix matches `ty::Adt(_, args) if ty.is_box()`, derives both `args.type_at(0)` and `args.type_at(1)`, and combines checks with `||`, labeling the two recursions `"{}boxed "` and `"{}allocator "`.
analysis.inputDomain: Rust async code compiled with the `must_not_suspend` lint enabled (the test uses `#![feature(must_not_suspend, allocator_api)]` and `#![deny(must_not_suspend)]`), where a `Box<T, A>` using a custom allocator `A` is live across an `await`, and `A` is declared `#[must_not_suspend]`. The regression input is `let x = Box::new_in(1i32, MyAllocatorWhichMustNotSuspend); suspend().await; drop(x);` with `MyAllocatorWhichMustNotSuspend` implementing `Allocator`.
analysis.summary: Bug fix in the coroutine state-transform must-not-suspend lint: for `Box<T, A>`, the check previously recursed only into the boxed element `T` and ignored the custom allocator type `A`. The corrected code checks both generic arguments, reporting an allocator held across a suspend point.
analysis.trigger: A value of type `Box<T, A>` with a non-default/custom allocator `A` (constructed, e.g., by `Box::new_in`) is held across an `await` inside an `async fn`, and `A` (or something nested in it) carries `#[must_not_suspend]`; the lint must report the allocator, not just the boxed value.
preconditions: The crate enables `must_not_suspend` and, for the test, `allocator_api` (edition 2021 in the test).
The `async fn` binds the `Box<T, A>` before an `.await` and keeps it live across that suspend point.
The allocator type `A` is annotated `#[must_not_suspend]` (directly or through nested types reachable by the recursive check).
The coroutine state-transform code runs the `check_must_not_suspend_ty` box arm rather than treating the ADT generically.
pitfalls: Using `ty.boxed_ty()` on a boxed ADT yields only the element type and loses the allocator type argument, so the allocator is silently unchecked.
For `Box<T, A>`, the allocator is `args.type_at(1)`; checking only index 0 misses it. Both checks should be combined with `||` so either argument can trigger the lint.
The diagnostic description prefix matters: the test expects an `allocator`-prefixed message, so the allocator recursion uses the `"{}allocator "` prefix rather than reusing the boxed prefix.
Short-circuiting with `||` is intentional here; do not assume the allocator check also runs when the boxed-element check already failed.
analysis.testStrategy: Add a UI regression test (`tests/ui/lint/must_not_suspend/allocator.rs`) with `//@ edition: 2021`, `#![feature(must_not_suspend, allocator_api)]`, `#![deny(must_not_suspend)]`, a `#[must_not_suspend]` allocator implementing `Allocator` via `Global`, and an `async fn` that creates `Box::new_in` before `suspend().await`. Expect one error whose message names the allocator as being held across a suspend point, with the await span marked, and record it in the corresponding `.stderr` file.
evidence: If the Box has a custom allocator, then that will not be checked at all.

error: allocator `MyAllocatorWhichMustNotSuspend` held across a suspend point, but should not be
